_README: Hand-recorded model facts that cannot be derived from DSS. Identity, consumer edges and
current and historical decision cross-references are GENERATED into .index/models.tsv -- do not hand-edit that.
Metrics are transcribed from docs/prioritizer/FEATURE_AUDIT.md section 4 (m3-m7), TARGET_PRIORITIZER 6.4
(the m1-m3 ladder) and the archived decision log (m8). A blank means NOT MEASURED or not recoverable --
never a guess. `?` in the rendered table means exactly that.
DO NOT source feature lists from `dku ml settings`: it returns the CURRENT mltask state, not a
deployed version's config. m8 was trained in m7's mltask, so that call reports m8's features
under a feature count that still matches the name m7-f14. See tools/recipe_classes.json.

2026-08-26: seven retired saved models were deleted from the flow (recoverable from analysis I2csfIX2 / mltask krJwswcb). `name`, `lab_session` and `lab_id` were added here so .index/models.tsv can still list them -- the index is built from live DSS objects, so without this the ablation ladder would vanish from the index the moment the models were dropped.
_consumer_rule: A non-champion model should only be referenced by its own train_* / score_psplit_validation_m*
recipes, or by a recipe listed in ablation_consumers. Anything else is a live entry point left
behind on a retired model -- which is exactly what happened to score_persona_candidates, found
still on m3-f12 (cGPhBOGC) after the champion had moved to m7-f14.

The m1/m2/m3 scoring recipes predate the score_psplit_validation_m<N> naming and are declared above rather than pattern-matched. Declaring them keeps the detector sharp: a NEW consumer on a retired model still fires, because it will be neither declared nor name-matched.

hJLGoYn4.delta: +prox_kernel (chosen over prox_mean to avoid feeding the hub axis)
hJLGoYn4.verdict: CHAMPION -- first model whose gain survives a paired test: association t=+3.29 and tractability t=+2.56, both with ZERO ties over 668 diseases. Mechanism REFUTED (Spearman(module size, delta) = -0.003): it works and we cannot say why
hJLGoYn4.name: m7-f14

3RZ9a9kN.verdict: REJECTED despite scoring better -- AUPRC up (t=+3.42) but AUROC flat (t=-0.42), tractability flat-to-declining (@200 t=-1.34) and hub spread worse. An association gain not corroborated on the degree-matched axis is the signature of exploiting label bias. This is the case the adoption rule was written for
3RZ9a9kN.name: m8-f14-pm

SybkzSdu.verdict: NOT A PRIORITIZER MODEL, and DELETED 2026-09-03. It was an LLM_GENERIC_RAW agent object left behind when Wave 6 removed the Act 1 graph agent path: the code went, the object stayed. Verified unused before deletion -- the Target Prioritizer has no /api/graph/* route, the Graph Explorer webapp reaches an LLM directly via config.llm_id rather than through an agent, and no recipe or scenario referenced it. Retained as a row here so the ladder history stays complete; it never had prioritizer metrics.
